note: Fixed prices, agreed in writing before I start. No hourly surprises and no hidden fees. Prices are shown in USD and adjust to your region.

faq.q: Why hire one person instead of an agency?
faq.a: With an agency you brief whoever sells the work, and it gets handed to whoever builds it. Here it's the same person from the first call to launch — I do the design, the build and the automation, so nothing is lost between people and one person is accountable for the result. You also skip the account-manager layer, which is a lot of what you'd otherwise be paying for.

faq.q: Who actually does the work? Do you subcontract?
faq.a: It's me. No subcontracting and no passing it to a junior team — that's the point of hiring an individual rather than a studio, and it's why every round of feedback reaches the person who wrote the code. If a job needs a specialist I'm not the right fit for, I'll say so before you pay anything rather than quietly staff it.

faq.q: How do I know I can trust someone I found online?
faq.a: Check rather than take my word for it. I'm Top Rated on Upwork with 45 five-star reviews, and every review on this site is unedited. My open-source work is public too: Bibata has been downloaded over 1.4 million times and ships as a default cursor theme on Linux distributions whose maintainers I've never met. That's strangers running my work on their own machines.

faq.q: How much contact will I actually get?
faq.a: A written progress update every two days, whether or not there's something to show. You approve the wireframe before visual design, and the design before the build, so nothing arrives as a surprise at the end. No mystery and no silence.

faq.q: What do I end up owning?
faq.a: The code, the designs and the accounts are yours. Handover is a step in the process rather than a favour at the end: launch, the files, and a short training session so your team can run the site without me. I don't bill you for access to your own work.

faq.q: How do I know which plan I need?
faq.a: Tell me what you're building and I'll point you to the right one — usually on a single short call. You don't have to pick from this page alone.

faq.q: Why do some prices say "starting at"?
faq.a: The build price is fixed, but the final number moves with scope — page count, product count or how many screens you need. You get the exact figure in a written proposal before any work begins.
Half up front to book your slot, half on launch. Monthly plans are billed at the start of each month and you can cancel any time.
Third-party costs — domains, hosting fees, paid Shopify apps, stock images and premium fonts — are billed at cost. I'll list any of these in the proposal so there are no surprises.

faq.q: Can you take over a site someone else built?
faq.a: Yes. I'll audit what's there first and tell you honestly whether it's better to fix it or rebuild it. The audit fee comes off the project if you go ahead.
